evals.prompt: I have a Go net/http service (Go 1.24, module github.com/acme/shop). Add OpenFeature feature flags to it using the flagd provider in RPC mode against a flagd at FLAGD_HOST/FLAGD_PORT. Requirements: (1) initialise the provider at startup and fail fast if it cannot connect; (2) a middleware that reads the X-User-Id header and makes it the targeting key for every flag evaluation in that request without passing context through every function by hand; (3) gate GET /checkout on the boolean flag `new-checkout` (old handler when off), logging the evaluation reason/variant at debug level; (4) graceful shutdown; (5) a unit test for the handler that does NOT need flagd running. Give me the code files.
evals.expected_output: Go code using github.com/open-feature/go-sdk/openfeature and go-sdk-contrib/providers/flagd/pkg: flagd.NewProvider(...) + openfeature.SetProviderAndWait; middleware using openfeature.WithTransactionContext(r.Context(), openfeature.NewEvaluationContext(userID, ...)); handler calling client.BooleanValueDetails(ctx, "new-checkout", false, openfeature.EvaluationContext{}) or Boolean; hooks.NewLoggingHook or logging of details.Reason/Variant; openfeature.Shutdown() on exit; test using memprovider.NewInMemoryProvider with InMemoryFlag variants.
assertions: Imports the real SDK package github.com/open-feature/go-sdk/openfeature (not a made-up path such as github.com/open-feature/go-sdk/pkg/openfeature)
Registers the flagd provider with openfeature.SetProviderAndWait (or SetProviderWithContextAndWait) and treats a non-nil error as fatal at startup
Uses the flagd provider constructor flagd.NewProvider(...) from github.com/open-feature/go-sdk-contrib/providers/flagd/pkg with host/port options or the FLAGD_HOST/FLAGD_PORT env-var auto-read

Middleware puts the X-User-Id value into transaction context via openfeature.WithTransactionContext(ctx, openfeature.NewEvaluationContext(userID, ...)) (or MergeTransactionContext) rather than threading an EvaluationContext argument manually
Handler evaluates `new-checkout` with a client method whose signature matches the SDK (Boolean / BooleanValue / BooleanValueDetails with ctx, key, default, EvaluationContext)
Evaluation reason/variant are logged at debug level, either via hooks.NewLoggingHook from go-sdk/openfeature/hooks or by logging BooleanValueDetails fields (Reason, Variant)
Calls openfeature.Shutdown() (or ShutdownWithContext) during graceful shutdown
Unit test uses memprovider.NewInMemoryProvider with memprovider.InMemoryFlag (State, DefaultVariant, Variants) so no flagd is needed
Does not invent APIs: no client.GetBooleanValue, no openfeature.NewProvider, no flagd.FlagdProvider{} struct literal, no ctx-less evaluation calls

evals.prompt: ASP.NET Core 8 minimal API (C#). Wire in OpenFeature with dependency injection: the flag backend speaks OFREP at the URL in the OFREP_ENDPOINT env var with a bearer token in OFREP_TOKEN. Add a hook that logs every evaluation. Add GET /pricing that reads the string flag `pricing-tier` (default "basic") with the signed-in user's name as targeting key and their `plan` claim as a context attribute, and returns the tier. Then write an xUnit test for the pricing logic that runs without any network using an in-memory flag set. Show Program.cs, the test, and the NuGet packages to add.
evals.expected_output: Program.cs with builder.Services.AddOpenFeature(fb => fb.AddHook(...LoggingHook...).AddProvider(sp => new OfrepProvider(new OfrepOptions(...){Headers=...})) or AddOfrepProvider(...)); IFeatureClient injected into the endpoint; EvaluationContext.Builder().SetTargetingKey(name).Set("plan", plan).Build(); await client.GetStringValueAsync("pricing-tier", "basic", ctx); packages OpenFeature, OpenFeature.Hosting, OpenFeature.Providers.Ofrep; test using InMemoryProvider with Flag<string> variants, either via Api.Instance.SetProviderAsync or an isolated Api, asserting the tier.
assertions: Adds the OpenFeature.Hosting package for DI and does NOT tell the user to add the deprecated OpenFeature.DependencyInjection package
Uses builder.Services.AddOpenFeature(fb => ...) and does not call the obsolete AddHostedFeatureLifecycle()
Registers the OFREP provider from OpenFeature.Providers.Ofrep (OfrepProvider / OfrepOptions or AddOfrepProvider) with the base URL and an Authorization: Bearer header taken from environment variables
Adds the built-in LoggingHook (OpenFeature.Hooks) through the builder (AddHook) or an equivalent custom Hook subclass with the correct BeforeAsync/AfterAsync/ErrorAsync/FinallyAsync signatures
The /pricing endpoint injects IFeatureClient (not Api.Instance.GetClient()) and calls GetStringValueAsync("pricing-tier", "basic", ctx) or GetStringDetailsAsync
Evaluation context is built with EvaluationContext.Builder().SetTargetingKey(...).Set("plan", ...).Build()
The xUnit test uses InMemoryProvider with a Flag<string> (variants dictionary + default variant) and needs no network
If the test uses Api.Instance, it awaits SetProviderAsync before evaluating (or uses an isolated Api / the DI container); it does not evaluate before the provider is set
Does not invent APIs: no GetStringValue without Async, no OpenFeature.SetProvider static, no EvaluationContext constructor with a dictionary, no Flag<string> without variants

evals.prompt:
We upgraded our FastAPI service from openfeature-sdk 0.9.x to 0.10.0 (flagd provider, openfeature-provider-flagd 0.5.x). Since then every flag evaluates to the default at startup with reason ERROR, and sometimes for the first few requests. Relevant code:

```python
from openfeature import api
from openfeature.contrib.provider.flagd import FlagdProvider
from openfeature.evaluation_context import EvaluationContext

api.set_provider(FlagdProvider(host="flagd", port=8013))
client = api.get_client()
client.set_evaluation_context(EvaluationContext(attributes={"service": "orders"}))

SHOW_BANNER = client.get_boolean_value("show-banner", False)

@app.get("/orders")
async def orders(request: Request):
    user = request.headers.get("X-User-Id")
    if client.get_boolean_value("new-orders-page", False, EvaluationContext(user)):
        ...
```

What changed, what is wrong with this code, and how should it look? We also want the user id applied to all evaluations in the request without passing it everywhere.
evals.expected_output: Explains that 0.10.0 made api.set_provider non-blocking (init in background thread) so evaluations right after it return defaults with PROVIDER_NOT_READY; fix with api.set_provider_and_wait(...) in a lifespan/startup hook or a PROVIDER_READY handler; SHOW_BANNER evaluated once at import is wrong (static + before ready); client.set_evaluation_context does not exist — set client.context or pass context per call; use ContextVarsTransactionContextPropagator + api.set_transaction_context in FastAPI middleware for the user id; check get_boolean_details().error_code; optionally get_boolean_value_async; api.shutdown() on lifespan exit.
assertions: Identifies that in openfeature-sdk 0.10.0 api.set_provider() became non-blocking (initialization runs in a background thread) so evaluations made immediately after it return the default with error code PROVIDER_NOT_READY
Recommends api.set_provider_and_wait(...) (or waiting on a PROVIDER_READY event handler) during application startup, e.g. in a FastAPI lifespan/startup handler
Points out that evaluating SHOW_BANNER at import/module level is wrong (runs before the provider is ready and never re-evaluates) and moves evaluation into request handling

States that client.set_evaluation_context(...) does not exist in the Python SDK and gives a working alternative (client.context = EvaluationContext(...), or api.set_evaluation_context for global, or per-call context)

Shows request-scoped targeting via api.set_transaction_context_propagator(ContextVarsTransactionContextPropagator()) at startup plus api.set_transaction_context(EvaluationContext(targeting_key=user_id, ...)) in a FastAPI middleware, so handlers need not pass the user id
Recommends inspecting details (client.get_boolean_details(...).error_code / .reason) or a PROVIDER_ERROR handler to confirm the diagnosis instead of guessing

Uses correct import paths and names: from openfeature import api; from openfeature.contrib.provider.flagd import FlagdProvider; from openfeature.transaction_context import ContextVarsTransactionContextPropagator; EvaluationContext(targeting_key=..., attributes=...)
Mentions api.shutdown() on application shutdown
Does not invent APIs (no api.wait_for_ready, no client.set_context, no FlagdProvider(url=...), no await api.set_provider)
